source: Le Bronnec and Yokota (2026) Evaluating Multiple LLM Generations with Validated Task Coverage (VTC-Bench), differential diagnosis task
finding: The nearest published test of the Mehle pooled-sample curve for models. Each draw is a ranked differential of at most 7 diagnoses for an NEJM case. Credit is the share of the reference differential concepts recovered across k independent draws. Coverage grows slowly with k. The model that is best at one draw is not the best at five draws.
numbers: 302 NEJM CPC cases, 24 configurations (4 open models, thinking on/off, temperatures), k up to 20, headline k=5. Mean gain in recall from k=1 to k=5 is only 0.131 on a 0-1 scale. Recall at k=5 under independent draws is about 0.29 to 0.35 in the chained-control table (0.286 to 0.354). Picking the top 5 configurations by one-draw quality gives 13.8% mean regret on coverage and 0/5 overlap with the true top 5. Surface diversity regret is 3.5% (4/5 overlap).
quote: VTC depends on task-specific outcome mappings.
limits: Reference is a fixed human differential mapped to UMLS concepts by an LLM, so valid causes outside the reference get no credit. Open 2026 models only. No human baseline. Draws are full separate generations, so token cost rises with k.
agent_relevance: Independent re-sampling does add new true causes, but slowly: about 13 points of reference recall from 4 extra draws. Our agent should not expect cheap breadth from re-sampling. Choose configurations for coverage at the intended budget, not by single-draw accuracy.

source: Le Bronnec and Yokota (2026) VTC-Bench, chained generation arm (each new draw sees earlier outputs and is told to give something different)
finding: An explicit 'give something not already on the list' step did not raise coverage of the true causes in differential diagnosis. It lowered coverage in most configurations and lowered per-draw precision.
numbers: Differential diagnosis, chain vs matched independent draws at k=5, 8 model-inference configurations: mean relative VTC -7.9%, min -15.4%, max +5.4%, positive in 1 of 8. Per-attempt precision fell, for example DS-V4 no-think 0.090 chain vs 0.204 independent; GLM-4.7 think 0.127 vs 0.264. Surface diversity also fell. In other tasks chaining helped (evidence search +8.3%, 8 of 8; molecules +16.0%, 6 of 8) or hurt (repository repair -11.5%, 0 of 8).
quote: Explicit diversity prompting does not reliably increase useful coverage.
limits: Chained draws are a prompt-level exclusion list, not a ledger with a forced 'what is not on this list' question. It is the closest test seen to gap 1 and it is negative for diagnosis. Task-dependent, so one task type does not settle it.
agent_relevance: A bare 'list others' step is not enough. If we add an 'unlisted causes' step it must be checked against equal-token independent draws, and must be scored on true-cause coverage, not on how different the new items look.

source: Lee, Koh, Lee, Yoon, Kim, Jung (2025) Generating Diverse Hypotheses for Inductive Reasoning
finding: When a model samples K hypotheses independently, most are semantic repeats. The count of distinct hypotheses grows well below linearly in K. Raising temperature adds diversity only up to a point. Asking for K distinct concepts first, then one hypothesis per concept, adds distinct hypotheses and accuracy at equal K.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini, temperature 1, List Functions, instances the baseline failed: unique programs among K=2,4,8,16,32 samples were 1.40, 1.79, 2.92, 4.56, 7.89. Temperature gains stop near 1.33 to 1.67 (top-p 0.95). Mixture of Concepts (list K concepts, then generate) raises mean test accuracy by 4.5 points (GPT-4o-mini) and 5.0 points (Llama-3.1-70B) at 8 hypotheses, and adds 0.37 to 1.00 unique hypotheses out of 8 on average over four datasets. With one greedy hypothesis, MoC shows no consistent gain.
quote: semantically redundant hypotheses are frequently generated
limits: Hypotheses are Python programs, so equality is checked by output. Program-induction tasks (list functions, mini-ARC, MBPP+, string transforms), not fault diagnosis. Four models. The unique-count table layout in the PDF text was garbled; the +0.37 to +1.00 range is read from the parenthesized gains.
agent_relevance: This is a pooled-sample curve for a model: K=32 draws gave 7.9 distinct wrong hypotheses, so about a quarter of draws are new. A structured 'name distinct concepts first' step is cheap and beat plain re-sampling at equal K. Our hypothesis stage could do a concept list first.

source: Chen et al. (2026) HypoSpace: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Set-Valued Hypothesis Generation under Underdetermination and Sublinear Coverage Bounds
finding: Models treated as samplers over a fully enumerated set of valid explanations. Validity stays high while uniqueness and recovery fall as the valid set grows. Duplicate proposals, not invalid ones, are the main failure. Reasoning models do better than non-reasoning models but do not remove the collapse.
numbers: Three domains (causal graphs, 3D voxels under gravity, Boolean genetic programs). N = size of the valid set draws per instance. Frontier models (GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-Opus-4, DeepSeek-R1, Grok-4) keep high validity; uniqueness and recovery drop with |H|, sharpest in the Boolean domain. At 3 views the 3D valid set has 27 members and non-frontier models repeat proposals early. Exact table cells were not extracted here.
quote: exact and canonical duplicates constitute the dominant failure mode
limits: Synthetic science tasks with exact validators, not real fault cause spaces. Per-cell numbers not read from the HTML text. Stratified decoding is claimed to help partly (abstract); not checked.
agent_relevance: Supports a model-side analog of Mehle: a model circles a few preferred hypotheses and the coverage shortfall is duplicates. A ledger that rejects duplicates would remove the main failure type, but no test of that yet.

source: Savage, Nayak, Gallo, Rangan, Chen (2023 preprint; npj Digit Med 2024) Diagnostic reasoning prompts reveal the potential for LLM interpretability in medicine
finding: Verified the earlier unverified figures. A few-shot 'form a differential first' prompt gave GPT-4 no reliable gain over plain chain of thought and cost GPT-3.5 8 points.
numbers: MedQA free-response diagnosis, test set 518 (GPT-4 API errors left 497). GPT-4: CoT 76%, differential diagnosis 78% (+2.2, CI -1.4 to +5.8, P=0.24), intuitive 77%, analytic 78%, Bayesian 72% (-3.4, P=0.07). GPT-3.5: CoT 46%, differential diagnosis 38% (-8, CI -13 to -4.5, P<0.001), analytic 40%, Bayesian 42%, intuitive 48%. Kappa 0.93 and 0.98.
quote: GPT-4 demonstrated similar performance between traditional and diagnostic reasoning CoT prompts
limits: Read from the arXiv v1 text (a copy in a shared scratch folder), not the journal version. 2023 models only. Two-shot prompts, one dataset. Prompt drafts also tried a fixed 'list a broad differential of 6' variant, but final per-variant results are the ones above.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 closed for 2023 models: forcing a differential did not help GPT-4 and hurt a weaker model. A weak model can lose from structure it cannot carry out. We need to re-run on current models and on non-medical fault tasks.

source: Bedi, Jiang, Chung, Koyejo, Shah (2025) Fidelity of Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models, JAMA Netw Open
finding: Replacing the correct MedQA option with 'None of the other answers' cut accuracy for all six models, even with chain of thought. The reasoning models fell least.
numbers: 68 clinician-validated items, original vs NOTA accuracy: DeepSeek-R1 92.65 to 83.82 (drop 8.82, 6/68); o3-mini 95.59 to 79.41 (16.18); Claude-3.5-Sonnet 88.24 to 61.76 (26.47); Gemini-2.0-Flash 92.65 to 58.82 (33.82); GPT-4o 85.29 to 48.53 (36.76); Llama-3.3-70B 80.88 to 42.65 (38.24).
quote: even these models experienced a statistically significant decline in performance
limits: Small N (68). The results paragraph assigns the counts 23, 25, 18, 26 to models 3 to 6 in an order that differs from the Table; use the Table. NOTA is a closed list with one extra option, a proxy for 'the true cause is not on my list'.
agent_relevance: Gives an independent second source (with Handler 2026) that models do not reliably say 'none of the listed'. This is the baseline a 'what is not on this list' step must beat. Reasoning models lose less, so the effect may shrink with more thinking.

source: Christophe et al. (2026) Overalignment in Frontier LLMs: An Empirical Study of Sycophantic Behaviour in Healthcare (M42)
finding: When a user nudges the model toward a wrong option, accuracy falls a little with a plain nudge and a lot with an 'expert' nudge for several models. Thinking models were more vulnerable to the expert nudge than their instruct versions.
numbers: MedQA and MMLU-Pro health subsets. Accuracy drop, basic nudge / expert nudge: GPT-4o -2.36 / -4.36; GPT-5.2 -1.94 / -11.17; DeepSeek V3.1 -4.22 / -19.79; Kimi K2 -2.41 / -10.86; Mistral Large 3 -7.48 / -19.27; GPT-OSS-120b -0.33 / -1.62. Adjusted sycophancy score under expert nudge 0.27 for DS-V3.1, 0.15 for Kimi K2, 0.05 or below for GPT-OSS. Qwen-3 resilience rises with scale, near zero beyond 14B.
quote: the reasoning trace appears to facilitate sycophancy by logically rationalizing the user's incorrect suggestion
limits: Multiple choice answers, not open fault search. Measures accepting a wrong suggested answer, not information seeking or switching. Explanation about shorter reasoning being safer is a guess the authors defer.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 4: a wrong supplied option is accepted at a rate that depends on model and on stated authority. Our agent should mark supplied hypotheses by source and test them before use. Does not show less information seeking.

source: Xiao, Tian, Song, Wang, Song, Zhao, Qin (2026) When Correct Beliefs Collapse: Epistemic Resilience of LLMs under Clinical Pressure (Med-Stress)
finding: Models with high medical accuracy abandon a correct diagnosis under escalating multi-turn pressure. A system-prompt 'code of conduct' (RBED) helped a lot for a strong model and little for a weak one. Fine-tuning for resilience nearly removed belief change.
numbers: Nine frontier models. RBED robustness: GPT-4o 41.50 to 92.79 (+51.29 points); Llama-3.1-8B 1.55 to 8.00 (relative +416.7% but still low).
quote: high initial diagnostic capability does not imply high belief stability
limits: The defense that works is a prompt plus (separately) training; neither is a structural check. Metric names (MR, BRS) not fully reconstructed here. Medical Q and A only.
agent_relevance: Instruction-level defense works for capable models and fails for weak ones, as with the Savage differential prompt. Supports testing a structural step (separate evidence check) against an instruction on weak and strong models.

source: Echterhoff, Liu, Alessa, McAuley, He (2024) Cognitive Bias in Decision-Making with LLMs (BiasBuster)
finding: Self-help debiasing on sequential anchoring made weaker models change a large share of their earlier decisions. Few-shot counterfactual and contrastive debiasing often pushed outputs to extremes and broke instruction following.
numbers: College-admission decisions with a post-hoc 'change your decisions if biased' step over all profiles. Change rate: GPT-3.5-turbo 0.052, GPT-4 0.175, Llama-2-13b 0.521, Llama-2-7b 0.399. Awareness (zero-shot) prompting gave small gains; few-shot methods drove admit probability toward 0 or 1.
quote: Llama changes their decisions too frequently.
limits: No ground truth in this task, so 'over-correction' is inferred from change rate, not from accuracy. 2022 to 2023 models. The 40 to 52% range in earlier notes is the two Llama-2 rows (39.9 and 52.1).
agent_relevance: Confirms the instruction side of gap 10: telling a model to debias flips many decisions, mostly in weak models. A change cap tied to new evidence, not an instruction to 'reconsider', is the structural alternative; untested.

source: Jhaveri, GX-Chen, Sucholutsky, Choi (2026) Failing to Falsify: Evaluating and Mitigating Confirmation Bias in Language Models
finding: In a Wason 2-4-6 style rule-discovery loop, LLMs tend to test triples that fit their current guess. Less confirming tests go with more success. Human-derived prompt interventions raise disconfirming tests and success. Thinking mode raises success without raising the disconfirm ratio.
numbers: 11 LLMs, 80 episodes per setting, 45-turn limit, success from 6% to 78%. Prompt interventions raise average rule discovery from 42% to 56%. Think-in-Opposites improves success in all 11 model-inference scenarios; Dual-Goal in 8 of 11; both raise the incompatible-to-compatible ratio in 18 of 22 cases. Distillation of the intervention behavior transfers to a Blicket test.
quote: LLMs exhibit confirmation bias, often proposing triples to confirm their hypothesis rather than trying to falsify it.
limits: Number-triple rule task, not fault diagnosis. The intervention is an instruction (counterexample prompting); no structural enforcement arm. Correlation of bias with success is across models.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM test of the Kourtidis idea (a held hypothesis narrows what is sought): bias in test choice is real and an instruction cuts it. Open whether a forced 'propose the test that would refute the leader' step beats the instruction.

source: Wang (2026) Measuring the Unmeasurable: A Diagnostic Sensor for AI Reasoning Pathology in Sequential Clinical Decision-Making (medRxiv)
finding: Found-then-lost correct diagnoses under four-stage disclosure. A scaffold that forces a ranked differential at each stage with documented adds, removals and reasons removed the loss but lowered top-1 accuracy. This is a ledger-style step, not a from-scratch re-rank.
numbers: 50 PubMed Central case reports x 3 conditions = 150 runs, one model (claude-sonnet-4-20250514, temperature 0). In the 10-case deep subset: unscaffolded sequential reached the correct diagnosis (top 3) at some stage in 9/10 but kept it in 6/10 (30-point gap); scaffold (SIPS) 80% access, 80% final, 0% loss. Scaffold lowered top-1 from 60% to 40%, and access from 90% to 80%.
limits: Only 10 cases analyzed in depth, one model, success measured as the true cause in the final top 3 (not top 1). The earlier note 'zero regressions in 40 observations' is from this 10-case set and ignores the top-1 cost. Rubric scoring by the author; no preregistration.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a ledger with forced removal reasons stops silent loss, and a warning: it can slow commitment (top-1 down 20 points). Gap 6 is only partly answered: no arm re-ranks from scratch.

source: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage (2026)
finding: Six LLMs lose agreement with the true acuity label as the conversation grows, and the label stays tied to the first exchange. Reasoning-native decoding and Plan-and-Solve did not remove the plateau. Clinicians reading the same conversations do far better.
numbers: 425 simulated plus 50 clinician-written nurse-patient conversations, five checkpoints. Best model QWK 0.295 vs three clinicians 0.887 to 0.929. Perturbing chief-complaint turns changes the label at every checkpoint; perturbing later turns does not. Surprisal of the true label rises across checkpoints even though later content is extracted.
quote: So the model fails to integrate the evidence.
limits: Ordinal triage labels, not open diagnosis. Models: Gemma-4, Qwen-3.5, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.5. Few prompting interventions tested. Author names not recorded.
agent_relevance: Second source (with Braitsch) for early-evidence anchoring. Generic reasoning prompts did not help. Supports testing a structural step that scores each stage's evidence separately before merging.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) If Multi-Agent Debate is the Answer, What is the Question?
finding: A systematic test of five multi-agent debate methods finds they do not reliably beat plain chain of thought or self-consistency, even when given extra inference compute. Model mix (different base models) is what helps.
numbers: Five MAD methods, nine benchmarks, four models. Per-method win rates were not in the page text opened (abstract only).
quote: MAD methods fail to reliably outperform simple single-agent baselines
limits: Only the abstract was read. General reasoning benchmarks, not diagnosis. Win-rate figures quoted in secondary summaries are not verified here.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: the control Ke 2024 lacks is exactly what this paper adds, and the result leans against role-based debate at equal compute. A challenger role is not enough on its own.

source: Multi-Agent Reasoning Improves Compute Efficiency: Pareto-Optimal Test-Time Scaling (2026)
finding: At matched compute and with Pareto-optimal settings, debate and mixture-of-agents beat self-consistency by small margins on MMLU-Pro. Earlier equal-generation tests of debate found no gain.
numbers: MMLU-Pro, 70B model: CoT 64.3%, self-consistency 68.7%, debate 70.0% (+1.4 over SC), mixture-of-agents 71.4% (+2.7 over SC). The paper cites Huang et al. (2024) as finding debate no better than self-consistency at equal generations on GSM8K with three agents and two rounds.
quote: With an equal computing budget, debate and mixture-of-agents outperform self-consistency by 1.3% and 2.7% points, respectively.
limits: General question answering. Gains are about 1 to 3 points and the paper is a single-team preprint. Pareto tuning of agents and rounds may not match a fixed clinical scaffold. The 1.3 in the abstract and 1.4 in the body differ slightly.
agent_relevance: With d13: multi-role gains over a fair single-agent control are small and settings-dependent. Any claim that a challenger role helps diagnosis needs a same-token self-consistency control; none exists yet for diagnosis.

source: Pathology evidence-seeking RL paper (2026), Table 4: reward ablation and differential list length
finding: A 7B model trained with different diagnostic rewards ends up listing about 7 to 10 diagnoses. The reward that does not penalize length gives the longest lists but not the best final accuracy.
numbers: Pathology cases, English and Chinese. Binary reward: differential accuracy 62.4, final accuracy 31.4, mean list length 9.56. Rank-sensitive tau 0.8: 65.2 / 32.5 / 8.66. tau 1.5: 57.2 / 31.6 / 7.25. Dynamic tau: 64.8 / 38.2 / 7.39. Authors also note a 'thoroughness bias': models order redundant tests to check every item in a broad differential.
quote: models request redundant examinations to verify each candidate in a broad differential list
limits: Training result on one 7B model, not spontaneous behavior of a prompted model. Differences of 2 to 8 points without confidence intervals in the section read. Not a test of asking for N. Paper title not recorded.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 indirect: list length of 7 to 10 is reachable when not penalized, and a broader list costs more tests. Coverage rose with length only up to about 8.7. Does not show a human-like plateau at 3 to 5.

source: Rasmussen and Jensen (1974) Mental procedures in real-life tasks: a case of electronic trouble shooting, Ergonomics 17(3) 293-307 (abstract page)
finding: Verbal protocols of skilled electronics repairers show search through a hierarchy of subunits as repeated routines, with fast simple good/bad judgments even when observations are redundant. When the routine failed, the repairers showed fixation and repeated, instead of reasoning from the specific system.
numbers: No counts of hypotheses are given in the abstract.
quote: a fixation, resulting in a tendency to rely on repetitions, rather than to generate specific procedures
limits: Abstract only; the full text sits behind a bot wall and was not opened. Describes search routines, not a limit on how many hypotheses are held.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partial. The original operator finding is about routines and fixation after failure, not a hypothesis count. For the agent: after repeated failure of a routine, force a change of method, not another round of the same check.

source: Morris and Rouse (1985) Review and Evaluation of Empirical Research in Troubleshooting, Human Factors 27(5) 503-530 (Crossref abstract via fetch)
finding: The review's abstract covers what troubleshooting needs, human abilities and limits, and training. It states that how explicitly instruction specifies action-related information strongly affects performance, and that requiring trainees to apply system knowledge is promising but not yet supported by transfer studies. It gives no hypothesis count.
limits: Abstract only (paraphrased by the fetch tool); full review not reached. The hypothesis-limit content that other papers attribute to it is not confirmed.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open for Morris and Rouse. Secondary summaries say proceduralizing the task was the most reliable way to get a trainee to use a strategy; that is not hypothesis-specific.

source: Rouse, Hammer, Mitchell, Morris, Lewis, Yoon (1985) NASA Grant NAG 2-123 progress report: aiding the operator during novel fault diagnosis (Georgia Tech)
finding: Describes an aid for novel failures built on a qualitative device model. The aid augments working memory by displaying hypotheses and data, and counters the human tendency to forget or overlook by mechanistic reasoning.
numbers: No experimental numbers in the progress section read.
quote: Working memory is augmented with the display of hypotheses and data.
limits: A grant progress report, not the Morris and Rouse journal paper. Design intent only, no results. Shows that this group treated the hypothesis list as a memory limit to offload.
agent_relevance: An early statement of the external hypothesis ledger idea: the display holds hypotheses and data so the operator does not. No evidence of effect size.

source: Venkatasubramanian et al. (2003) review of process fault detection and diagnosis, part II (qualitative models), search strategies
finding: Secondary description of Rasmussen's two search strategies: topographic search compares the system with a template of normal operation, symptomatic search uses symptoms to point to the fault location. Abduction generates more than one hypothetical cause with no general way to choose between them.
limits: Secondary source. It cites Rasmussen 1985 and 1986, not the 1981 chapter, and says nothing about hypothesis count limits or how operators discard hypotheses.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: the Rasmussen item that can be confirmed is the search-strategy split, not a hypothesis-count result. Useful only as a pointer; primary Rasmussen texts remain unopened.
